polls.pollster: Cornell University ILR School Center for Applied Research on Work (Empire State Poll; data collected by SSRS)
polls.mode: online (SSRS probability-based Opinion Panel n=1,005 blended with Dynata opt-in panel n=1,624), English and Spanish
polls.notes: Annual Cornell Empire State Poll, 2026 edition. Only this one news release has been published so far; no 2026 report, toplines or question wording found (CAROW Empire State Poll page lists 2024 and 2025 reports only). Margin of error not reported; blended probability/nonprobability sample. Release reports only the top four answers on the most-important-issue item, so that result list is partial. Figures are published to one decimal place. Release also gives 2024 comparisons (not recorded). The 40.3% "got worse and will keep getting worse" figure is a combination published by Cornell.

Published NET rows dropped; TOTAL rows kept as published. No NYC column in the crosstabs, so nyc_results is null. Personal-experience items Q3, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, Q11 (insurance holdings and ability to pay) were not recorded as questions. Q2 'Gun policy' and 'LGBTQ+ issues' each 1. questions.subject: Letting the attorney general sue oil and gas companies to recover home insurance costs
questions.wording: Home insurance rates are increasing, in part due to increasing extreme weather events. To address these rate increases, New York lawmakers are considering a bill that would allow the state Attorney General to sue the oil and gas industry to recover those costs, instead of insurers passing those costs onto New Yorkers. Do you support or oppose this proposal becoming law in your state?
questions.quote: two-thirds of New York voters (67%) support legislation that would allow the state attorney general to sue the oil and gas industry to recover home insurance cost increases — rather than letting insurers pass those costs onto New Yorkers. Just 24% oppose the proposal

questions.subject: State suing oil and gas companies for extreme weather damages

Knowing this, would you support or oppose your state suing oil and gas companies to hold them accountable for damages stemming from extreme weather disasters?

questions.subject: Letting the attorney general sue oil and gas companies to recover home insurance costs
questions.wording: Home insurance rates are increasing, in part due to increasing extreme weather events. To address these rate increases, New York lawmakers are considering a bill that would allow the state Attorney General to sue the oil and gas industry to recover those costs, instead of insurers passing those costs onto New Yorkers. Supporters of the bill say there is evidence that large oil and gas companies have known for decades that their products contribute to extreme weather events and climate change and that they misled the public about it. They argue that, for this reason, those companies should pay for rate increases. Having read more, do you support or oppose this proposal becoming law in your state?
questions.quote: When respondents first are presented with an argument in favor — that oil and gas companies have known for decades their products worsen extreme weather, and misled the public about it — support rises to 71% (+50-point net margin).

questions.subject: Letting the attorney general sue oil and gas companies to recover home insurance costs
questions.wording: Home insurance rates are increasing, in part due to increasing extreme weather events. To address these rate increases, New York lawmakers are considering a bill that would allow the state Attorney General to sue the oil and gas industry to recover those costs, instead of insurers passing those costs onto New Yorkers. Opponents of the bill say that oil and gas companies would simply pass any costs onto consumers through higher energy prices. They also say that climate change is a global problem, and it's unfair to single out only energy companies for weather events that everyone contributes to. They argue that, for this reason, those companies should not be made to pay for rate increases. Having read more, do you support or oppose this proposal becoming law in your state?
questions.quote: When respondents are then presented with an argument in opposition — that companies will simply pass costs through to consumers via higher energy prices — a majority of voters (58%) still support the bill.

polls.notes: Business Council 'affordability campaign' survey on energy bills. bcnys.org blocks automated fetches (403 via WebFetch and curl); the release text (field dates, n, MOE, mode, Tunnl as pollster) was read from the Wayback Machine copy (web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.bcnys.org/news/poll-new-yorkers-demand-bill-transparency-and-relief-energy-costs-steadily-skyrocket). The chart deck PDF downloaded directly from bcnys.org; it starts at slide 6, so its methodology slides are not in the file. Results read from chart labels on rendered slides (deck slides 10, 15, 17, 18, 26, 27); quotes are the slide headline/question text plus the chart values as labeled. Deck breaks results by Urban/Suburban/Rural, not NYC, so nyc_results is null. Bill-literacy items (familiarity with charges, who approves rates, transparency) not recorded. The release's '53% understood rising costs are largely driven by factors outside a utility's control' refers to slide 21 after an informational prompt; not recorded. On slide 27 two small segment labels overlap ('6%3%', '8%2%'); values were read as 6/3 and 8/2 (those rows sum to 100; the public-cost-estimate row sums to 99 as published).
